title: They’re still both better than Sentimental Man tho 🫢 #Wicked #WickedF...
transcript: Let's talk about the original songs in wicked for good, specifically girl in the bubble and No Place Like Home. There are a few other new musical moments in the film, but I want to focus specifically on the two new full songs. I'll start with no place like home, cause I think that's the one that felt the most additive. It is a completely new moment that does not exist in the stage show, where Elphaba is explaining her perspective on why she continues to fight this fight and trying to convince the animals fleeing Oz not to flee and to stay and fight with her. And while I don't think it necessarily tells us anything we didn't already know about Alphabet as a character, this whole notion of should you leave or stay and fight? I think it's actually really interesting. The movie does kind of frame it as if leaving is the wrong choice, which I found a little bit questionable. But I did overall like the scene and liked getting insight from the animals themselves as to how they were feeling about everything going on in Oz. But I thought this song itself is just fine. Although I did like seeing a more softer side to Alphabet compared to, like, Defying Gravity and no good Deed. I think that Stephen Schwarzman easily could have written her just another song where she belts her face off, and I'm glad he resisted that impulse. Moving on to girl In the bubble, I also think this song is just fine, but its place in the movie feels far less justified. It really hindered the pacing in my opinion, coming directly in the middle of March of the Witch Hunters. Ariana Grande obviously sings and performs it beautifully, and I do get why they felt like Glinda deserved a song in this moment. It's a really important realization for her character. But there is also a reason why this song doesn't exist in the original musical. There just really isn't time for it.
